objects.description: Abstract interface for managing crash diagnostics in Hermes VM. Allows registering memory regions and key/value custom data to be included in crash dumps, registering crash-time callbacks that write JSON to a file descriptor, and recording heap usage info. Implementations decide how dumps are produced and where output is written.

Plain data struct nested in CrashManager capturing heap state at a moment: used_ is the number of bytes currently in use; size_ is the number of bytes available before a full GC is triggered. Passed to CrashManager::setHeapInfo for recording.

Concrete no-op implementation of CrashManager. All operations are inert; registering callbacks returns key 0, and recorded data is discarded. Useful as a default or for testing when crash reporting is disabled.

objects.definition: using CallbackKey = int;
objects.description: Alias type for identifiers returned when registering crash callbacks with CrashManager. Represents the handle used to unregister callbacks. Pointer form shown here per requirements; the underlying type is int.

objects.definition: using CallbackFunc = std::function<void(int fd)>;
objects.description: Alias for the function object type invoked after a crash. Receives a file descriptor to which a JSON object should be written. Implementations route the FD appropriately.

Abstract interface (exported) provided to GC tripwire callbacks to request heap snapshots. It defines a virtual destructor and two pure virtual methods to capture a heap snapshot either to a file path or to an output stream. Construction is via implementations elsewhere; this header only declares the interface.

objects.definition: class ProgramState;
objects.description: Forward declaration of a class representing debugger-visible program state. Only an incomplete type is provided here; definition is not present in this header.

objects.definition: using String = std::string;
objects.description: Alias for UTF-8 encoded strings used by the debugger API. When originating from JavaScript, valid UTF-16 surrogate pairs are decoded and unmatched halves are replaced with U+FFFD.

objects.definition: using BreakpointID = uint64_t;
objects.description: Unsigned 64-bit identifier type for debugging entities like breakpoints. 0 is invalid (see kInvalidBreakpoint).

objects.definition: using ScriptID = uint32_t;
objects.description: Unsigned 32-bit identifier for a loaded script within a single VM invocation. Not reused within a VM run.
Value type describing a source file position: 1-based line and column, script identifier, and filename. Fields default to kInvalidLocation when unspecified.
Value type describing a single stack frame: the executing function name and the current source location.

Represents a sequence of call frames captured from current execution or an exception. Constructible internally by friends; public API exposes read-only accessors for frame count and retrieval by index.
Value type describing an exception: textual description, throw location, and associated stack trace (read-only accessor). Stack trace is set internally by the debugger.
Enumeration of reasons why execution paused in the debugger (e.g., script load, debugger statement, breakpoint, step completion, exception, async pause, or eval completion).
Enumeration of stepping modes: into, over, or out of function calls.
Enumeration specifying when to pause on exceptions: never, on uncaught only, or on all throws.
Enumeration distinguishing implicit async pauses (internal transfer of values) from explicit user-requested pauses.

objects.definition: using ScopeDepth = uint32_t;
objects.description: Unsigned 32-bit depth index into a lexical scope chain, counting from outermost or implementation-defined order as used by the debugger.
Value type exposing counts of variables per lexical scope. Internally stores a vector of per-scope variable counts and provides read-only queries. Contents are populated by the debugger.
Value type describing a breakpoint: unique ID, enabled flag, resolution status, and requested versus resolved locations.

Exception type (derives from std::runtime_error) thrown to signal an out-of-memory condition in the Hermes VM. Constructor is private (accessible only to GCBase via friendship), implying users cannot directly instantiate it; destruction is virtual and defined out-of-line. Intended to be thrown by GC/allocator internals; catch as std::runtime_error or JSOutOfMemoryError.
Enumeration selecting the VM’s compilation strategy: default smart heuristics, forced eager compilation, or forced lazy compilation.
Strongly-typed enum controlling synthetic tracing behavior: disabled, replaying, tracing, or both tracing and replaying. Underlying type is int8_t.

objects.definition: class PinnedHermesValue;
objects.description: Forward declaration of a class representing a GC-pinned Hermes value. Only an incomplete type is provided in this header; full definition resides elsewhere.

objects.definition: _HERMES_CTORCONFIG_STRUCT(RuntimeConfig, RUNTIME_FIELDS, {})
objects.description: Configuration struct for initializing a Hermes VM runtime instance. The concrete definition is generated by the _HERMES_CTORCONFIG_STRUCT macro using the RUNTIME_FIELDS list in this header. Fields include GCConfig, RegisterStack, MaxNumRegisters, NativeStackGap, JIT/Eval/Intl/Proxy feature toggles, tracing and sampling settings, compilation mode, generator enablement, crash manager, and experiment flags. Exact member layout depends on the macro expansion defined in hermes/Public/CtorConfig.h.

Represents a JavaScript function frame within a sampled call stack, including function name, script ID, and optional source URL and definition line/column. String fields are string_view references into storage owned by the containing Profile.
Represents a native Hermes engine function frame (e.g., built-ins) in a sampled call stack, storing the native function name by string_view into external storage.
Represents a host/integrator-provided native function frame (e.g., console.log) in a sampled call stack, with the function name held by string_view into external storage.
Represents a VM suspension frame in the call stack (GC, Debugger, or Multiple). Encapsulates the suspension kind.
Enumeration of suspension frame subtypes for ProfileSampleCallStackSuspendFrame: GC, Debugger, or Multiple.

objects.definition:
using ProfileSampleCallStackFrame = std::variant<
    ProfileSampleCallStackSuspendFrame,
    ProfileSampleCallStackNativeFunctionFrame,
    ProfileSampleCallStackHostFunctionFrame,
    ProfileSampleCallStackJSFunctionFrame>;
objects.description: Type alias for a variant representing any supported call stack frame type captured in samples: suspend, native, host, or JS function frames.
A single sampled snapshot consisting of a timestamp, thread ID, and a call stack captured as a vector of ProfileSampleCallStackFrame elements. Provides iteration helpers and counts.

Owns the sampled profiling trace: a chronologically ordered vector of ProfileSample and a unique_ptr to a string storage deque that backs the string_view fields in frame objects. Non-copyable but movable; samples and frames must not outlive the Profile due to string storage ownership.

functions.name: hermes::vm::CrashManager::registerMemory
functions.description: Registers a block of memory to be included in any crash dump that occurs. Call unregisterMemory with the same pointer before freeing that memory.
requirements: mem must point to allocated, valid memory at the time of registration and until it is unregistered.
The same mem pointer must be unregistered via unregisterMemory(mem) before the memory is freed.
length represents the number of bytes controlled by mem (must match the actual allocation size).
Thread-safety and lifetime ownership beyond the above are unknown (not specified).

functions.name: hermes::vm::CrashManager::unregisterMemory
functions.description: Unregisters a previously registered memory block so it is no longer included in crash dumps.
requirements: mem should be a pointer that was previously passed to registerMemory (inferred from API pairing).
Behavior for pointers that were not registered is unspecified (not documented).

functions.name: hermes::vm::CrashManager::setCustomData
functions.description: Associates a custom key/value string pair to be included in any crash dump. Repeated calls with the same key overwrite the prior value.
requirements: key is a C-string tag used to distinguish values; must be a valid null-terminated string pointer (inferred from type).
val is the value to store; must be a valid null-terminated string pointer (inferred from type).
Setting the same key more than once overwrites the previous value.

functions.name: hermes::vm::CrashManager::removeCustomData
functions.description: Removes any custom data associated with the specified key from future crash dumps. If the key was never set, this is a no-op.
requirements: key must be a valid null-terminated string pointer (inferred from type).
It is valid to call this even if key was never set; the call is a no-op as documented.

functions.name: hermes::vm::CrashManager::setContextualCustomData
functions.description: Associates a custom key/value string pair only for the current thread to be included in crash dumps.
requirements: key must be a valid null-terminated string pointer (inferred from type).
val must be a valid null-terminated string pointer (inferred from type).
Data set is scoped to the current thread (as documented); cross-thread visibility should not be assumed.

functions.name: hermes::vm::CrashManager::removeContextualCustomData
functions.description: Removes thread-local contextual custom data associated with the key set via setContextualCustomData for the current thread.
requirements: key must be a valid null-terminated string pointer (inferred from type).
Only affects data set with setContextualCustomData for the calling thread (as documented).

functions.name: hermes::vm::CrashManager::registerCallback
functions.description: Registers a function to be invoked after a crash to serialize diagnostic information as JSON to a provided file descriptor. Returns a key that can be used to unregister the callback.
requirements: callback must be callable with signature void(int fd), where fd is a raw file descriptor to which the callback should write a JSON object (as documented).
The returned CallbackKey must be retained by the caller to later unregister the callback via unregisterCallback(key).
The destination and handling of the fd are implementation-defined; the callback should not assume more than a writable file descriptor (as documented).
Behavior and constraints of executing in a post-crash environment (e.g., async-signal-safety) are not specified; callers should avoid assumptions (unknown).

functions.name: hermes::vm::CrashManager::unregisterCallback
functions.description: Unregisters a previously registered crash callback identified by key so it will no longer be executed during a crash.
requirements: key must be a CallbackKey previously returned by registerCallback on the same CrashManager instance (inferred from API).
Behavior for invalid or unknown keys is unspecified (not documented).

functions.name: hermes::vm::CrashManager::setHeapInfo
functions.description: Records the current heap usage information to be included in crash diagnostics.
requirements: heapInfo must describe the current heap state; used_ is the currently used bytes; size_ is the bytes available before a full GC (as documented).
Thread-safety and frequency of calls are not specified (unknown).

functions.name: hermes::vm::CrashManager::~CrashManager
functions.description: Virtual destructor for CrashManager. Ensures proper cleanup via base-class pointer deletion. Concrete implementations may provide cleanup logic.
requirements: No specific caller requirements beyond standard object lifetime management.
Must be called implicitly/explicitly when destroying a CrashManager instance.

functions.name: NAME::rebuild
functions.description: Returns a Builder initialized with the current configuration state of NAME. Use when you want to start from an existing NAME instance and modify some fields via the Builder API before rebuilding.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, fully-constructed NAME instance.
Returned Builder references a copy of the current config (by value stored in Builder).

functions.name: NAME::doBuild
functions.description: Applies BUILD_BODY logic to finalize or validate the configuration during build(). This is invoked internally by Builder::build() and is not intended to be called directly by users.
requirements: builder must be a valid Builder associated with the same NAME type.
Any constraints/validation are defined by BUILD_BODY (unknown to this macro).

functions.name: NAME::Builder::Builder
functions.description: Default constructor for the Builder. Initializes an empty builder with no fields marked explicitly set and a default-constructed internal NAME config_.
requirements: None beyond default constructibility of all fields and NAME.

functions.name: NAME::Builder::Builder
functions.description: Constructs a Builder seeded from an existing NAME configuration. Subsequent withX() calls modify a copy of config.
requirements: config must be a valid NAME instance.

functions.name: NAME::Builder::build
functions.description: Finalizes and returns the NAME configuration. Calls NAME::doBuild(*this) to run any BUILD_BODY logic, then returns the internal config_ by value.
requirements: May invoke validation or mutation defined in BUILD_BODY; callers should expect that constraints may be applied.
After calling build(), the returned NAME is independent of the Builder.

functions.name: NAME::Builder::update
functions.description: Updates this builder with explicitly set fields from newConfig. For each field where newConfig.hasField() is true, copies that field into this builder.
requirements: newConfig must be a Builder for the same NAME type.
Only fields marked explicitly set in newConfig are updated; others are ignored.

functions.name: hasNAME
functions.description: Indicates whether the field NAME was explicitly set on the Builder via withNAME(). Generated per-field inside NAME::Builder.
requirements: Must be called on a NAME::Builder instance.
The specific field identifier (NAME) must correspond to a declared field in the FIELDS list.

functions.name: getNAME
functions.description: Getter on the NAME configuration class returning the current value of the field NAME. Generated per-field on the config type.
requirements: Callable on a constructed NAME instance.
TYPE corresponds to the declared type of the field NAME in FIELDS.

functions.name: getDefaultNAME
functions.description: Returns the default value for the field NAME as declared in FIELDS. CX is a macro parameter typically used to inject qualifiers like constexpr.
requirements: Only valid if the field NAME has a default that is brace-initializable as written in FIELDS.
CX must be a valid token sequence for the intended qualifier (e.g., empty or constexpr) when the macro is expanded.
TYPE corresponds to the field’s declared type.

functions.name: withNAME
functions.description: Sets the Builder’s field NAME to the provided value and marks it explicitly set. Returns *this to allow chaining (fluent API). Value is moved into the config.
requirements: Must be called on a NAME::Builder instance.
Argument must be convertible to TYPE; it will be moved into storage.
Subsequent hasNAME() will return true for this field.

functions.name: hermes::vm::GCTripwireContext::~GCTripwireContext
functions.description: Virtual destructor for GCTripwireContext. Allows deletion via a base-class pointer when a GC tripwire callback provides a GCTripwireContext instance. No return value; cleans up derived implementations.
requirements: The GCTripwireContext object must be a valid, live instance when destroyed.
Destruction should occur according to normal C++ object lifetime rules (do not use after destruction).

functions.name: hermes::vm::GCTripwireContext::createSnapshotToFile
functions.description: Captures the current heap to a file. Intended to be called from within a GC tripwire callback to persist a snapshot for later analysis. Returns an empty std::error_code on success; otherwise a non-empty error code describing the failure.
requirements: path: path to save the heap capture; it should designate a file location writable by the process (inferred from purpose).
Callers must check the returned std::error_code; success is indicated by an empty (default-constructed) error code.
The GCTripwireContext instance must be valid when called.
This function is pure virtual; it requires a concrete implementation provided by the runtime.

functions.name: hermes::vm::GCTripwireContext::createSnapshot
functions.description: Captures the current heap to a provided output stream. Intended for use in a GC tripwire callback to stream a snapshot to a caller-controlled destination. Returns an empty std::error_code on success; otherwise a non-empty error code.
requirements: os must be a valid std::ostream that is ready for writing; it must remain valid for the duration of the call (inferred from parameter type and purpose).
captureNumericValue controls inclusion of numeric values in the snapshot; exact semantics are not documented here (unknown).
Callers must check the returned std::error_code; success is indicated by an empty (default-constructed) error code.
The GCTripwireContext instance must be valid when called.
This function is pure virtual; it requires a concrete implementation provided by the runtime.

functions.name: facebook::hermes::debugger::StackTrace::callFrameCount
functions.description: Returns the number of call frames contained in this StackTrace. Use to size or iterate over frames from top (index 0) downward.

functions.name: facebook::hermes::debugger::StackTrace::callFrameForIndex
functions.description: Returns the CallFrameInfo at the given index, where 0 is the topmost (current) frame. Useful for iterating or inspecting a specific frame.
requirements: index must be less than callFrameCount(); otherwise access will throw std::out_of_range due to use of vector::at().
Callers should be prepared to handle std::out_of_range if passing unvalidated indices.

functions.name: facebook::hermes::debugger::ExceptionDetails::getStackTrace
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the StackTrace associated with this exception. Use to inspect frames where the exception occurred.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the originating ExceptionDetails object remains alive.
The returned reference is const; callers must not attempt to modify the stack trace.

functions.name: facebook::hermes::debugger::LexicalInfo::getScopesCount
functions.description: Returns the number of lexical scopes described by this LexicalInfo. Use to iterate scopes from depth 0 to depth getScopesCount()-1.

functions.name: facebook::hermes::debugger::LexicalInfo::getVariablesCountInScope
functions.description: Returns the number of variables declared in the specified lexical scope depth.
requirements: depth must be less than getScopesCount(); otherwise access will throw std::out_of_range due to use of vector::at().
Callers should be prepared to handle std::out_of_range if passing unvalidated depths.

functions.name: hermes::vm::JSOutOfMemoryError::~JSOutOfMemoryError
functions.description: Destructor for hermes::vm::JSOutOfMemoryError, an exception type derived from std::runtime_error used to signal out-of-memory conditions in Hermes VM code. It cleans up the exception object when it goes out of scope (e.g., after being caught) or is otherwise destroyed. Typical users should not call this directly; the class is intended for internal use by the Hermes VM (construction is private and restricted to friends). Other behavioral details (e.g., noexcept) are not specified in the header and are unknown.
requirements: Destructor is non-public (no explicit access specifier in class, defaulting to private); callers must not attempt to directly invoke or delete an instance unless they have appropriate access (e.g., are friends of the class).
Instances of JSOutOfMemoryError cannot be constructed by general callers (constructor is private); creation and corresponding destruction are intended to be managed internally by Hermes VM.
No parameters and no return value; there is nothing for callers to supply.
Exception-safety guarantees (e.g., whether the destructor is noexcept) are not stated; treat as unknown.

import os
import random
from typing import List

# Generator for an arbitrary binary blob intended to back std::string storage
# used as a memory region in NopCrashManager::registerMemory/unregisterMemory.
# Constraints from the fuzz stub:
# - Buffer must be non-empty (length > 0), as the stub bails on empty.
# - Any bytes are allowed, including NULs; returned as bytes.
# - Interesting cases: various sizes (small/medium/near page), diverse byte patterns,
#   and alignment-friendly lengths since the stub may cast data() to void*.

_MAX_SIZE = 4096

def _choose_sizes(rng: random.Random) -> List[int]:
    # Prefer a spread of sizes, with bias toward common interesting boundaries.
    candidates = [
        1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64,
        127, 128, 255, 256, 511, 512, 1023, 1024, 1536, 2048, 3072, 4095, 4096
    ]
    # Random size in range as well
    candidates.append(rng.randint(1, _MAX_SIZE))
    # Pick one size from candidates
    return [rng.choice(candidates)]

def _pattern_fill(size: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Select a content strategy to produce valid yet varied buffers.
    strategies = [
        "zeros",
        "ones",
        "increment",
        "decrement",
        "random",
        "repeated_byte",
        "ascii_text",
        "alternating",
        "page_boundary_mix",
    ]
    strat = rng.choice(strategies)

    if strat == "zeros":
        return b"\x00" * size
    if strat == "ones":
        return b"\xFF" * size
    if strat == "increment":
        return bytes((i % 256 for i in range(size)))
    if strat == "decrement":
        start = rng.randrange(256)
        return bytes(((start - i) % 256 for i in range(size)))
    if strat == "random":
        return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(size))
    if strat == "repeated_byte":
        b = rng.randrange(256)
        return bytes([b]) * size
    if strat == "ascii_text":
        # Generate printable ASCII with occasional NULs and newlines to exercise C-string-ish consumers.
        alphabet = [
            *range(0x20, 0x7F), # printable
            0x0A, 0x0D, 0x09,   # lf, cr, tab
            0x00               # NUL
        ]
        return bytes(alphabet[rng.randrange(len(alphabet))] for _ in range(size))
    if strat == "alternating":
        a = rng.randrange(256)
        b = rng.randrange(256)
        if b == a:
            b = (a + 1) % 256
        out = bytearray(size)
        for i in range(size):
            out[i] = a if (i & 1) == 0 else b
        return bytes(out)
    if strat == "page_boundary_mix":
        # Mix different patterns around 4K-ish boundaries to model potential real buffers.
        out = bytearray(size)
        # Regions: head, middle, tail
        thirds = max(1, size // 3)
        regions = [
            (0, min(thirds, size)),
            (min(thirds, size), min(2*thirds, size)),
            (min(2*thirds, size), size),
        ]
        fills = [
            lambda n: bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n)),
            lambda n: bytes((i % 256 for i in range(n))),
            lambda n: b"\x00" * n,
        ]
        for idx, (s, e) in enumerate(regions):
            if e <= s:
                continue
            chunk = fills[idx % len(fills)](e - s)
            out[s:e] = chunk
        return bytes(out)
    # Fallback random
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(size))

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Determine a single buffer size adhering to max limit and non-empty.
    size = _choose_sizes(rng)[0]
    size = max(1, min(size, _MAX_SIZE))
    data = _pattern_fill(size, rng)
    # Ensure non-empty invariant
    if not data:
        data = b"\x00"
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets inputs consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR() in the provided stubs.
# The stubs exercise:
#  - CrashManager/NopCrashManager custom data APIs (keys/values as C-strings)
#  - Sampling profiler frame/profile constructors (function names, URLs)
#  - Debugger ExceptionDetails text and filenames
# These fields expect valid, null-terminated C-strings on the C++ side. FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# will read the entire buffer as a sequence of strings. We therefore emit a sequence
# of length-prefixed strings that the harness can split, with rich variation to drive
# different code paths (optional URL presence, varied sizes, character sets).
#
# Format we produce (self-describing):
#   [count:1 byte]
#   repeated count times:
#     [len:2 bytes little-endian]
#     [payload bytes of that length]
#
# Each payload is a UTF-8 capable byte sequence without embedded NUL to be safe as
# C-strings. We diversify content by including:
#  - short/medium/long names
#  - plausible JS function names
#  - plausible URLs
#  - filenames and paths
#  - numeric-like strings
#  - unicode strings (encoded in UTF-8)
#  - empty strings
# We cap total output to <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

JS_IDENT_START = string.ascii_letters + "$_"
JS_IDENT_BODY = JS_IDENT_START + string.digits


def _rand_js_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 24) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    if n <= 0:
        return ""
    s = [rng.choice(JS_IDENT_START)]
    for _ in range(n - 1):
        s.append(rng.choice(JS_IDENT_BODY))
    return "".join(s)


def _rand_url(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    schemes = ["http", "https", "file"]
    tlds = ["com", "org", "net", "local", "io", "dev"]
    host = _rand_js_ident(rng, 3, 10)
    tld = rng.choice(tlds)
    path_parts = [
        _rand_js_ident(rng, 0, 8),
        _rand_js_ident(rng, 0, 8),
    ]
    path = "/" + "/".join([p for p in path_parts if p])
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        # add filename with extension
        exts = ["js", "mjs", "ts", "jsx", "bundle", "min.js"]
        base = _rand_js_ident(rng, 1, 12)
        ext = rng.choice(exts)
        if "." in ext:
            fname = base + ext  # already contains .
        else:
            fname = f"{base}.{ext}"
        if path.endswith("/"):
            path += fname
        elif path == "/":
            path = "/" + fname
        else:
            path += "/" + fname
    q = ""
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        q = f"?v={rng.randint(1,9999)}&cache={rng.choice(['on','off'])}"
    return f"{rng.choice(schemes)}://{host}.{tld}{path}{q}"


def _rand_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    roots = ["/tmp", "/var/log", "/home/user", ".", "..", "/"]
    base = _rand_js_ident(rng, 1, 12)
    exts = [".log", ".txt", ".json", ".js", ".map", ""]
    parts = [rng.choice(roots)]
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        parts.append(_rand_js_ident(rng, 1, 10))
    parts.append(base + rng.choice(exts))
    return "/".join([p.strip("/") for p in parts if p != "/"]).replace("//", "/")


def _rand_unicode_str(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 0, max_len: int = 64) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Choose from a mix: ASCII, Latin-1 supplement, some CJK, emoji
    chunks: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(n):
        t = rng.random()
        if t < 0.6:
            chunks.append(chr(rng.randint(0x20, 0x7E)))  # printable ASCII
        elif t < 0.8:
            chunks.append(chr(rng.randint(0x00A0, 0x00FF)))
        elif t < 0.95:
            chunks.append(chr(rng.randint(0x4E00, 0x9FFF)))  # CJK Unified
        else:
            # Emoji range sample
            chunks.append(chr(rng.choice([0x1F600, 0x1F602, 0x1F680, 0x1F4A9, 0x1F9E9])))
    return "".join(chunks)


def _make_string_pool(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    pool: List[bytes] = []
    # Ensure presence of key types used by stubs
    candidates: List[str] = []

    # Some keys/values for CrashManager
    base_keys = [
        "user_id", "session", "build", "env", "feature", "flag", "tag", "x", "k",
        "",  # empty key
    ]
    base_vals = [
        "123", "true", "false", "release", "debug", "canary", _rand_unicode_str(rng, 0, 24),
    ]

    for k in base_keys:
        candidates.append(k)
    for v in base_vals:
        candidates.append(v)

    # JS function names typical
    for _ in range(8):
        candidates.append(_rand_js_ident(rng, 1, 20))
        candidates.append(_rand_js_ident(rng, 1, 8) + ".anonymous")
        candidates.append(_rand_js_ident(rng, 1, 8) + "::" + _rand_js_ident(rng, 1, 8))

    # URLs and filenames
    for _ in range(5):
        candidates.append(_rand_url(rng))
        candidates.append(_rand_filename(rng))

    # Unicode-rich strings for ExceptionDetails text and filenames
    for _ in range(5):
        candidates.append(_rand_unicode_str(rng, 0, 40))

    # Numeric-like strings and edge cases
    candidates.extend([
        "0", "1", str(rng.randint(2, 1_000_000)),
        "-1", "9999999999", "0xdeadbeef", "NaN", "Infinity",
        "line:1 column:1", "col:999", "L" + str(rng.randint(1, 100000)),
    ])

    # Some long-ish names/paths but still under limits
    long_name = _rand_js_ident(rng, 50, 80)
    candidates.append(long_name)

    # Convert to bytes ensuring no embedded NUL; replace any NUL if produced (should not be)
    for s in candidates:
        if not isinstance(s, str):
            s = str(s)
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='replace').replace(b"\x00", b" ")
        pool.append(b)

    return pool


def _pack_strings(strings: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Prefix with count, then len (LE 2 bytes) + data.
    out = bytearray()
    count = min(len(strings), 255)
    out.append(count)
    total = 1
    for i in range(count):
        s = strings[i]
        if len(s) > 65535:
            s = s[:65535]
        # Ensure we do not exceed MAX_TOTAL; if so, stop.
        need = 2 + len(s)
        if total + need > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out += len(s).to_bytes(2, 'little')
        out += s
        total += need
    # If we broke early, fix the count
    out[0] = i if total <= MAX_TOTAL else max(0, (i))
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build an interesting pool and then sample a randomized subset to introduce variety per call
    pool = _make_string_pool(rng)

    # Randomize ordering and pick a subset length
    rng.shuffle(pool)
    desired = rng.randint(10, min(80, len(pool)))
    strings = pool[:desired]

    # Ensure presence of specific categories by possibly appending a few more crafted items
    # Empty string, a typical function name, and a URL
    extra = [b"", _rand_js_ident(rng).encode('utf-8'), _rand_url(rng).encode('utf-8')]
    for e in extra:
        if e not in strings:
            strings.append(e)

    return _pack_strings(strings)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for a buffer intended to seed FUZZ_PARAM_STR and related calls in the
# ProfileSampleCallStackJSFunctionFrame fuzzer stub. The stub requests:
# - One function name string (stored in deque and used as string_view)
# - One URL-like string (may be used depending on random bitmask)
# - An unsigned int r (bitmask to toggle optionals)
# - A uint32_t scriptId
# - Up to two more uint32_t values (for line and column), consumed regardless of bits in the stub
#
# We will pack data as a simple tagged textual format that FUZZ_PARAM_STR reads from
# sequentially via the fuzzer harness. Since we cannot control the harness directly,
# we provide a single bytes blob concatenating fields in order with clear separators.
#
# Layout (UTF-8 text):
#   functionName + "\n"
#   urlString + "\n"
#   r (unsigned int) in decimal + "\n"
#   scriptId (uint32) in decimal + "\n"
#   lineSeed (uint32) in decimal + "\n"
#   colSeed (uint32) in decimal + "\n"
#
# This format allows FUZZ_PARAM_STR to pull the first two strings, and integer
# parameters parsed from the underlying byte stream by the fuzzing engine.
# We ensure values are within reasonable ranges to exercise optional code paths.

URL_SCHEMES = [
    "http", "https", "file", "data", "blob", "ftp"
]

def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len=0, max_len=24) -> str:
    # JavaScript function-like names, may include unicode and dollar/underscore
    base_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_$"
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    if n == 0:
        return ""
    # First char cannot be a digit usually; bias to letter/_/$
    first = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + "_$")
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(base_chars) for _ in range(n - 1))
    # Occasionally produce an anonymous-like or unusual name
    choices = [first + rest, "", "<anonymous>", "λ" + rest[: max(0, n-1)]]
    return rng.choice(choices)


def _rand_url(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce a variety of plausible URLs to back scriptUrl; not strictly validated
    scheme = rng.choice(URL_SCHEMES)
    if scheme == "data":
        mime = rng.choice(["text/javascript", "application/javascript", "text/plain"])  
        payload = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "+/=") for _ in range(rng.randint(8, 40)))
        return f"data:{mime};base64,{payload}"
    if scheme == "file":
        parts = ["", "usr", "local", "lib", "hermes", "scripts"]
        tail = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-_") for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 12)))
        ext = rng.choice([".js", ".mjs", ".ts", ""])
        return f"file:///{'/'.join(parts)}/{tail}{ext}"
    if scheme == "blob":
        host = rng.choice(["", "http://localhost:3000", "https://example.com"])  
        uuid = '-'.join(''.join(rng.choice(string.hexdigits.lower()) for _ in range(n)) for n in [8,4,4,4,12])
        return f"blob:{host}/{uuid}"
    # http/https/ftp
    host_labels = [
        ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8)))
        for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4))
    ]
    host = '.'.join(host_labels)
    port = ":" + str(rng.randint(1, 65535)) if rng.random() < 0.2 else ""
    path_segs = [
        ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-_.$") for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 10)))
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 5))
    ]
    if not path_segs or rng.random() < 0.5:
        path_segs.append(''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8))) + rng.choice([".js", ".mjs", ".map", ""]))
    path = "/" + "/".join(path_segs)
    q = ""
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        kvs = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
            k = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6)))
            v = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_.") for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 8)))
            kvs.append(f"{k}={v}")
        q = "?" + "&".join(kvs)
    frag = "#" + ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 6))) if rng.random() < 0.2 else ""
    return f"{scheme}://{host}{port}{path}{q}{frag}"


def _rand_u32(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Return a uint32 value
    return rng.randrange(0, 2**32)


def _compose_fields(fn: str, url: str, r: int, script_id: int, line_seed: int, col_seed: int) -> bytes:
    # Ensure no embedded newlines to keep parser simple; replace with spaces
    fn_s = fn.replace('\n', ' ').replace('\r', ' ')
    url_s = url.replace('\n', ' ').replace('\r', ' ')
    parts = [fn_s, url_s, str(r), str(script_id), str(line_seed), str(col_seed)]
    data = "\n".join(parts) + "\n"
    b = data.encode('utf-8')
    # Keep under 4096 bytes
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
    return b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Create diverse function names: normal, anonymous, unicode, long
    fn = _rand_ident(rng, min_len=0, max_len=rng.randint(0, 48))

    # Generate URL-like string
    url = _rand_url(rng)

    # Bitmask r toggles presence of optional fields in the stub
    # Ensure we exercise all combinations across seeds: pick bits randomly with bias
    bits = 0
    if rng.random() < 0.8:  # often include url
        bits |= 1
    if rng.random() < 0.7:  # often include line
        bits |= 2
    if rng.random() < 0.6:  # often include column
        bits |= 4
    # Randomly sprinkle additional bits (ignored by stub but harmless)
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        extra = rng.randrange(0, 0xFFFF) << 3
        bits |= extra

    # ScriptId: small and large values
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        script_id = rng.randint(0, 5000)
    else:
        script_id = _rand_u32(rng)

    # Seeds for line/column; stub mods them into reasonable ranges
    line_seed = _rand_u32(rng)
    col_seed = _rand_u32(rng)

    return _compose_fields(fn, url, bits, script_id, line_seed, col_seed)
